changes: Mint with val(): private vector elements contain canonical uint32 values with an empty default constructor. Each new logical slot is assigned by the existing factorial/inverse-factorial computation before use. Initial element is initialized from Mint(1). No direct new expressions, owning pointers or custom allocator.

GCC excludingClang grows large tables (count>=4096 and capacity exceeded) by reserve, empty resize, std::copy initialized prefix and swap. Capacity uses same max(required,size+min(size,max_size-size)); allocation failure rollback remains. Clang/others use ordinary vector.resize because its existing relocation loop vectorizes efficiently.
Prepared COM arithmetic remains the original two Mint multiplications. Tables remain canonical residues; no Montgomery encoding or per-query modulus dispatch.

io_diagnostic.note: Diagnostic only, not a submission or replacement main. Preloads expected numeric answers before the clock, then reads the same input pairs and prints the correct full-width answers. Excludes preloading time. Does not prove an absolute lower bound; differs from interleaved memory arithmetic and may warm stream parsing caches.

notes: Earlier raw variant used custom copy on all compilers and is not final. Its Clang incremental-growth regressions led to compiler-specific vector growth.

Same-process copy followup did not reproduce earlier separate-binary copy regressions. Final focused prepare includes allocator/page effects and has systematic baseline/control differences; residuals remain recorded.
